A two-day, hands-on workshop for medical education faculty and researchers.
You will leave able to import a dataset, explore it, visualise it, tabulate it,
and wrap the whole thing in a document that regenerates itself — no
copy-pasting between R, Word and PowerPoint ever again.

::: {.callout-important}
## Before you arrive
Install R, RStudio and Quarto, then run the setup check. It takes about
30 minutes and saves an hour of Day 1.
→ [**Start here: Prelude**](prelude/index.qmd)
:::

## What you will be able to do

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card-tile}
### Work reproducibly
Organise a project so that a colleague — or you, six months later — can
rerun every number in your paper from raw data.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Visualise data
Build publication-quality figures with `ggplot2`, layer by layer, from a
grammar you can reason about rather than a menu you memorise.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Wrangle and explore
Use `dplyr` verbs to filter, group and summarise messy education data, and
run an honest exploratory analysis before you model anything.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Publish with Quarto
One `.qmd` source → HTML, Word, PDF, slides. Citations, cross-references and
figures that update when the data does.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Tabulate for journals
`gtsummary` for Table 1, comparisons and regression output that is
submission-ready in three lines of code.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Use GenAI honestly
Prompt engineering that helps rather than hallucinates — plus the ethical
and disclosure rules that apply to health research in India.
:::

:::

## Structure of the two days

| | Day 1 — Wed 9 Sep | Day 2 — Thu 10 Sep |
|---|---|---|
| **Morning** | Foundations, getting started, R & `ggplot2` | Communicating with Quarto, `gtsummary` |
| **Afternoon** | Quarto basics, `dplyr` & EDA | Generative AI, live coding, group work |

Every teaching block (45 min) is followed by a hands-on block (45–60 min).
Roughly two-thirds of your time is spent with your hands on a keyboard.

→ [Full schedule with timings and faculty](schedule.qmd)

## Who this is for

Medical education faculty and researchers who are **new to R**. No prior
programming assumed. If you have used SPSS, Excel or Stata, you already
understand most of the statistical ideas — this workshop changes the tools,
not the statistics.

## How to use this site

- **Prelude**: do this *before* the workshop.
- **Day 1 / Day 2**: one page per session: objectives, slides, worked
  examples, exercises with collapsible solutions.
- **Resources**: cheatsheets, troubleshooting, glossary, further reading.

All materials stay online after the workshop. The site is built from a public
repository; corrections are welcome as issues or pull requests.
